hypothesis: The swap-gain computation in the graph-cut partitioner recomputes cut contributions from raw adjacency but double-counts the exchanged edge (node1<->node2) because it is counted in both `node1_to_complement`/`node2_to_partition` before and again in `node1_to_partition`/`node2_to_complement` after; correcting the gain so the mutually-exchanged edge cancels exactly yields a more accurate min-cut refinement that reduces cross-tier cuts (and thus cross-tier detours), improving TNS across all circuits.
analysis: The hypothesis did not hold: total score is −0.107, with only 2/3 cases improving slightly and ariane133-ng45 regressing sharply (dWNS −9.3%, dTNS −16.4%). The mechanism claim (fewer cross-tier cuts → less detour → better TNS) is contradicted by ariane's large TNS loss despite overflow ~126, suggesting the gain correction perturbs partition balance or timing-critical assignments rather than cleanly reducing cuts. bp/bp_fe gains are marginal and within noise. Next step: instrument the partitioner to log actual cut-size deltas per move and correlate with per-path timing, isolating whether the exchanged-edge cancellation changes move acceptance or just gain sign.
